title: Shadow surge governor with cost- and latency-conditioned throttles
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: large shadow traffic bursts (spikes from canary seeding and replayed consumer traffic) can transiently blow through cost budgets or push latency p95s above SLOs even when user-facing traffic remains stable. Existing shadow lanes are either fully on or off and rely on global throttles; that makes short-lived surges noisy and causes blunt rollback decisions.

What this PR does (single-string description): Implements a lightweight 'shadow surge governor' that dynamically gates shadow traffic per-model and per-cohort using a combined cost and latency signal. The controller exposes two levers: (1) a soft throttle that reduces shadow fraction with a decay curve when cost burn exceeds a configured budget, and (2) an urgency gate that pauses shadow forwarding when latency SLOs (p95/p99) breach configured thresholds. The controller integrates with the rollout planner to surface a 'surge advisory' so canary and A/B orchestrators can preemptively throttle new promos rather than triggering full rollback.

Key features: 1) Per-model budget windows (sliding 1h/6h/24h) for cost and request-count; 2) latency-conditioned pause (configurable percentile and margin); 3) session-coherent decays so a user's in-flight shadow session is not dropped mid-request; 4) simulated dry-run mode that runs the throttle policy on mirrored traffic and emits an estimated cost/latency delta to the rollout planner; 5) a lightweight replay verifier that runs sampled shadow requests through a canary variant in a sandbox to detect regressions before a throttle decision triggers rollback; 6) telemetry hooks for Console: predicted burn, throttle factor, and advisory signals.

Compatibility and scope: Works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Uses existing shadow mirror pipeline and rollout APIs; adds a small runtime sidecar to handle session coherence for Private installs where kernel-level network mirroring is not available. No model format changes.

Testing and rollout plan: Unit tests for policy math; e2e with the canary orchestrator in benchmark-lab using synthetic surge traces; phased rollout behind a feature flag with a 0%->10%->50% canary of internal traffic. Monitoring dashboards and alerting thresholds added to the Console playbook.

Why it's different from previous work: Prior PRs implemented static shadow quotas or global throttles. This PR ties throttle decisions to both cost budgets and latency SLOs and surfaces advisory signals directly to rollout orchestrators so the system can perform gentle throttles instead of blunt rollbacks. It also prioritizes session coherence and includes a sampled replay verifier to avoid false positives from noisy upstream infra.

review_conversation: Evan Chen (2026-02-11): Can we ensure the throttle math is stable with heavy downsampling? In particular I'm worried about oscillation when p95 temporarily recovers. Requested change: add hysteresis window to the urgency gate.

Author (Priya) (2026-02-12): Added a 15s hysteresis by default and made it configurable per-deployment. See policy/decay_policy.go changeset. Also added tests that simulate oscillatory latency patterns.

release_notes:
Introduces shadow surge governor: dynamic, cost- and latency-conditioned throttles for shadow traffic; dry-run advisory mode for rollout planners; replay verifier for sampled checks. Default off behind feature-flag.

Impact: improves stability of staged rollouts by preventing transient shadow spikes from causing unnecessary rollbacks. Admins should review Console playbooks for new metrics and adjust cost budgets as needed.
